WoW: Forever

Mage

Mage is a cloth caster with no self-heal whose answers to trouble are Frost Nova, Blink and Polymorph. Forever added a Research and scroll system from level 6, and gave Arcane two new spells, Arcane Blast and Missile Barrage, Fire a Pyroblast it can cast inside a fight, and Frost Ice Lance.

WoW: Forever · Updated October 5, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70124 · Null Ossuary

Written for levelling, 1 to 60. Forever's beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Mage build has been tested. Ability training levels below come from foreverchanges.pro's reading of the beta client. Note that caster base damage was cut across the board and spell coefficients raised to compensate, a lower tooltip number than Classic is usually not a nerf. Neither Wowhead nor ClassicWoW.gg publishes a levelling score for the three specs. Icy Veins is the only one of the three that rates them, and it gives both a number out of five and a heading; those are reported on each spec's own page.

Which spec?

SpecRoleIts strongest pointIn one line
ArcaneRanged DPSArcane Meditation keeps 50% of mana regeneration running while you cast, where Classic gave 15%Arcane Blast and Missile Barrage, both new — ClassicWoW.gg: "build around Arcane-school damage itself"
FireRanged DPSWake of Fire takes 2 seconds off Fire Blast and gives the next one after a kill +50% critHeating Up (renamed from Hot Streak on October 1) cuts Pyroblast's cast from 6 seconds to 1.5 at 3 stacks
FrostRanged DPSFrostbite 3/3 gives every Chill effect you apply a 15% chance to freeze the target outrightFreeze, then Ice Lance for +300%. Icy Veins: "slowing and chilling everything they fight keeps them safe"

The three specs do different things. Arcane is the genuinely new one: Forever gave it Arcane Blast and Missile Barrage, neither of which existed in Classic, and Arcane Meditation at 50% mana regeneration while casting against Classic's 15% — Icy Veins names that talent as what "significantly reduces downtime between fights". Fire is the critical-strike spec: Heating Up from 25 makes Pyroblast castable inside a fight, and Ignite returns 40% of a spell's damage again over 4 seconds. Frost freezes: Frostbite gives every Chill effect a chance to lock the target down, and Ice Lance hits a frozen target for +300%.

Each spec page carries Icy Veins' levelling score and its heading for that spec, which is the only rating any of the three tracked sources publishes.

One claim worth flagging rather than stating flat: none of the three sources confirms or denies a target cap or damage falloff on Mage area spells in Forever. Treat that as genuinely open rather than settled either way. The slows attached to area damage were cut hard, though; Improved Blizzard maxes at 40%, down from Classic's 65% (ClassicWoW.gg's talent tooltip: rank 3 reads "lowers the target's movement speed by 40% for 1.5 sec").

Is Mage for you?

Play Mage if you want burst damage from range and can accept cloth armour, no self-heal and a mana bar you have to manage. (Our own reading, not a source's.)

Strengths

  • Ice Lance hits a frozen target for +300%, and Heating Up makes Pyroblast castable inside a fight from 25
  • Conjures its own drink from level 4 and food from level 6, so neither is ever bought
  • Polymorph at level 8 takes one enemy out of a fight entirely

Weaknesses

  • Cloth armour, and the only armour spells are Frost Armor, Ice Armor at 30 and Mage Armor at 34
  • Mana regeneration stops while you cast until Mage Armor at 34 or Arcane's Arcane Meditation, both 50%
  • No self-heal of any kind

New to this class?

Is the rotation simple? The published level 20 rotations run five or six steps: a nuke, a freeze, a retreat, a wand finish.

Is it forgiving? No. You have cloth armour, no self-heal, and mana that does not regenerate while you cast.

What carries you while levelling? Conjured drink from level 4 and food from level 6, so you buy neither, and Polymorph from 8 takes one enemy out of a fight.

Does it need a group? No. Every spec has a published solo build, and Arcane and Frost also have published dungeon variants.

Levelling milestones

LevelWhat you get
1Fireball, Frost Armor, Arcane Intellect, now 1 hour
4Frostbolt, Conjure Water
6Fire Blast, Conjure Food, and Comprehend Scroll plus the Study skill, new in Forever
8Arcane Missiles, Polymorph
10Frost Nova, your first real control
14Arcane Explosion, first area power spike
16Flamestrike, second
20Blink, Evocation, Blizzard, Mana Shield, and the four capital teleports
24Counterspell
28Conjure Mana Agate
30Ice Armor
34Mage Armor, now returns 50% of regeneration while casting, was 30%
40The four portals, Frostfire Bolt, new, mount
50Teleport: Dalaran, new — Gnome, Human and High Order Skyborne only

Detect Magic is the only Mage spell deleted in Forever. Frostfire Bolt is checked against the lower of the target's frost and fire resistance and counts as both schools, which may make it replace Fireball outright for a fire mage.

Which race

Read this section in proportion. Race is the smallest of the choices on this page, well behind spec, gear and knowing your rotation, and no race is a wrong answer for levelling (ours, not a source's). Where racials genuinely decide things is PvP, and specifically the ones that break crowd control: Will of the Forsaken (Undead, fear, sleep and charm), Escape Artist (Gnome, roots and snares) and Stoneform (Dwarf, bleeds, poisons and disease). A free trinket slot is worth more than any damage racial below.

Alliance — Human or Gnome. Human's Sword Specialization is +2% spell and ability crit off a sword held purely as a stat stick, which is a real change to the vanilla answer, though compare it honestly against a staff with better stats, because at levelling levels the staff often wins. Gnome brings Expansive Mind and Eureka!, but as of October 1 Eureka! no longer benefits periodic effects at all — a channeled cast like Arcane Missiles or Evocation doesn't count as a periodic, so those still get the bonus, but a damage-over-time tick (Fire's Ignite, for instance) no longer does. (Known issue: Eureka currently doesn't affect every damaging or healing spell for some classes; Blizzard says it's fixed in a later build.)

Horde — Orc is new to Mage in Forever, and Blood Fury now gives +10% spell power, so it is finally a caster racial. Its axe racial is dead weight, since Mages cannot use axes.

Skyborne Mage is Alliance-only. Troll's Berserking is now a flat +10% cast speed, and Undead's Cannibalize restores mana as well as health.

Quality of life

  • Conjured water is free drink from level 4, upgrading through the gem ladder, so there is never a reason to buy it.
  • Teleports come from a separate portal trainer standing near your class trainer, and every teleport consumes a Rune of Teleportation at about nine and a half silver. Slow Fall eats a Light Feather per cast, carry a stack of both.
  • Pick up books from level 6. Forever's new Research system unlocks from finding books in the world and returning them to librarians, and it pays real gear, a ring for twenty book donations, and a pendant from its quest. Failing to decipher a scroll turns you into a sheep until your skill improves. (Known issue, October 1: some Mages who learn Research find themselves locked out of accessing it — that's a bug, not something you did; it's worth knowing before you chase it early.)
  • Every Comprehension scroll lost move-casting on October 1. All Mage scrolls from the Research system had a balance pass and can no longer be cast while moving — budget the stand-still time like any other cast.
  • Get a wand early and use it instead of Fire Blast.

What changed from Classic

ChangeWhat it means for you
Ice Lance added as an 11-point Frost talentFreezing things is now a damage engine, not just an escape
Arcane Blast added to Arcane, Heating Up to FireArcane gained a main nuke of its own, and Fire a Pyroblast it can cast inside a fight
The slows on area damage were cut hardImproved Blizzard is 40% at max rank, down from 65%. Kiting needs more room
Whether area damage keeps a target cap is unconfirmedNone of the three tracked sources states it either way for Forever
Detect Magic deletedThe armours are Frost, Ice and Mage. There is no Molten Armor, and there never was in Classic either
Research, scrolls and Comprehension added at 6An entirely new system, easy to miss
Mage Armor returns 50% regen while castingWas 30%

At level 60

Unknown. No source publishes a Mage build past 30, so whether Arcane's new engine holds up, whether Fire takes over once Pyroblast is usable, and how far the scroll system goes are all untested. Raids open December 9.

Sources

Compiled from the three major Forever guide sites and cross-checked against each other. Where Blizzard has published an official class deep dive, that post outranks all three and the page is written from it. Everything else — talent ranks, tooltip values, what exists in the tree at all — is settled against the client itself, read through foreverchanges.pro and wago.tools. Where the guides disagree with each other, this page says which said what.
